newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK aims to close boatpeople riot camp by January.
newsitem.headline: HK aims to close boatpeople riot camp by January.

text.p: Hong Kong said on Thursday it would next month shut a large detention camp for Vietnamese boatpeople that was ravaged by fierce riots earlier this year.

The government said in a statement it was also confident that all other camps would be closed by the time Britain hands the territory back to China, at midnight next June 30, with its drive to repatriate failed asylum seekers gathering pace.
"Should the current rate of repatriation continue, it should be possible to close all Vietnamese migrant camps in the territory by mid 1997," the government statement said.
The Whitehead detention centre, which held up to 25,000 boatpeople at its peak in October 1991, would be closed on January 3.
More than 61,000 boatpeople have been repatriated to Vietnam since 1989, and there are now about 7,700 still left in the territory.

China resumes sovereignty over Hong Kong on July 1 next year and has insisted that the British colonial government empty the boatpeople camps by that time. The detainees are the last of a huge exodus of people who fled Vietnam after the communists won the war there in 1975.
